page: Given epsilon > 0, choose delta = min(1, epsilon / (2|a| + 1)).
f is uniformly continuous on A if for every epsilon > 0 there is some delta > 0 such that for all x, y in A, |x - y| < delta implies |f(x) - f(y)| < epsilon.
Theorem. If f is continuous on [a, b], then f is uniformly continuous on [a, b].
The order of the quantifiers matters: delta is chosen after epsilon and after a.
Long-term potentiation (LTP) is a persistent strengthening of synapses based on recent patterns of activity, dependent on NMDA receptor activation.
Neurons communicate through synapses. Neurotransmitters are released from vesicles, cross the synaptic cleft, and bind receptors on the postsynaptic membrane. Reuptake and enzymes clear them.
